healthInformationSourcesScreen.title: Health information sources
healthInformationSourcesScreen.intro: This app provides health and nutrition information based on established scientific research. The following sources are used for calculations and recommendations:
healthInformationSourcesScreen.disclaimer: This app is for informational purposes only and cannot replace professional medical advice. Always consult healthcare professionals for personalized medical guidance.

bmi.title: BMI Calculation (Body Mass Index)
bmi.description: BMI is calculated from weight and height to estimate weight status. This index is a screening tool only and does not replace a personalized medical assessment.

cdc.title: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
cdc.citation: Calculating BMI using the English system and metric system. CDC Growth Chart Training.

bmr.title: BMR Calculation (Basal Metabolic Rate)
bmr.description: We use the Mifflin-St Jeor equation to calculate basal metabolic rate, considered the most accurate method for healthy individuals.

mifflin.title: Mifflin MD, St Jeor ST, Hill LA, Scott BJ, Daugherty SA, Koh YO.
mifflin.citation: A new predictive equation for resting energy expenditure in healthy individuals. Am J Clin Nutr. 1990;51(2):241-7.

roza.title: Roza AM, Shizgal HM.
roza.citation: The Harris Benedict equation reevaluated: resting energy requirements and the body cell mass. Am J Clin Nutr. 1984;40(1):168-82.

activity.title: Activity Level Factors
activity.description: Physical activity factors are applied to BMR to estimate total daily energy expenditure based on established research.

brooks.title: Brooks GA, Butte NF, Rand WM, Flatt JP, Caballero B.
brooks.citation: Chronicle of the Institute of Medicine physical activity recommendation: how a physical activity recommendation came to be among dietary recommendations. Am J Clin Nutr. 2004;79(5):921S-930S.

iom.title: Institute of Medicine (US) Panel on Macronutrients.
iom.citation: Dietary Reference Intakes for Energy, Carbohydrate, Fiber, Fat, Fatty Acids, Cholesterol, Protein, and Amino Acids. Washington (DC): National Academies Press (US); 2005.

macros.title: Macronutrient Distribution
macros.description: Recommended macronutrient ratios are based on nutrition guidance from health organizations.

dietaryGuidelines.title: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and U.S. Department of Agriculture.

who.title: World Health Organization.
who.citation: Diet, nutrition and the prevention of chronic diseases. WHO Technical Report Series, No. 916. Geneva: WHO Press; 2003.

nutrients.title: Nutrient Daily References
nutrients.description: Daily reference amounts for fiber, sugar, saturated fat, trans fat, cholesterol, sodium and potassium follow the FDA Daily Values; sugar and trans fat limits follow WHO guidelines.

fda.title: U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
fda.citation: Daily Value on the Nutrition and Supplement Facts Labels.

whoSugars.title: World Health Organization.
whoSugars.citation: Guideline: Sugars intake for adults and children. Geneva: World Health Organization; 2015.

whoFats.title: World Health Organization.
whoFats.citation: Saturated fatty acid and trans-fatty acid intake for adults and children: WHO guideline. Geneva: World Health Organization; 2023.

weightManagement.title: Weight Management
weightManagement.description: Weight loss and weight gain recommendations are based on evidence-based methods for sustainable weight management.

wadden.title: Wadden TA, Webb VL, Moran CH, Bailer BA.
wadden.citation: Lifestyle modification for obesity: new developments in diet, physical activity, and behavior therapy. Circulation. 2012;125(9):1157-70.

hall.title: Hall KD, Heymsfield SB, Kemnitz JW, Klein S, Schoeller DA, Speakman JR.
hall.citation: Energy balance and its components: implications for body weight regulation. Am J Clin Nutr. 2012;95(4):989-94.

acceptance.body: By using Check Calo, you agree to follow the terms and conditions described in this document.

planExplain.title: How we got these numbers
planExplain.dailyBmr: At rest your body burns about {{bmr}} kcal a day (BMR, Mifflin-St Jeor formula from your age, gender, height and weight).
planExplain.dailyTdee: Your activity level ({{activity}}) multiplies that by {{factor}}: about {{tdee}} kcal a day keeps your weight where it is.
planExplain.dailyLose: Eating {{gap}} kcal less than that each day gives your target of {{kcal}} kcal.
planExplain.dailyGain: Eating {{gap}} kcal more than that each day gives your target of {{kcal}} kcal.
planExplain.dailyMaintain: Since you want to hold your weight, your target is exactly that.
planExplain.weeklyLose: About {{perKg}} kcal equals 1 kg of body fat, so a {{gap}} kcal weekly deficit loses about {{rate}} kg a week, a {{pace}} pace.
planExplain.weeklyGain: About {{perKg}} kcal builds 1 kg, so a {{gap}} kcal weekly surplus adds about {{rate}} kg a week, a {{pace}} pace.
planExplain.weeklyMaintain: Eating a bit more one day and a bit less the next keeps you steady.
planExplain.weeklyFlex: The weekly total matters most: a heavier meal one day can be balanced over the next few.
planExplain.targetNow: Today you weigh {{weight}} kg, a BMI of {{bmi}} ({{category}}).
planExplain.targetThen: At {{weight}} kg your BMI will be {{bmi}} ({{category}}).
planExplain.targetMaintain: You will keep this weight and BMI.
planExplain.targetHealthy: A BMI of 18.5–24.9 is considered a healthy range for adults.
planExplain.dateMath: {{change}} kg at {{rate}} kg a week takes {{weeks}}, so around {{date}}.
planExplain.dateMaintain: Maintaining has no finish line: keep eating around your target and weigh in now and then.
planExplain.dateEstimate: This is an estimate. Weight moves day to day with water and salt, so the app follows the trend of your weigh-ins and adjusts along the way.
planExplain.macrosSplit: Protein {{protein}}g ({{proteinPercent}}%) · Fat {{fat}}g ({{fatPercent}}%) · Carbs {{carbs}}g ({{carbsPercent}}%) of your daily calories.
planExplain.macrosWhy: Protein is set from your body weight to protect muscle and keep you full; fat covers essential needs, and carbs fill the rest for energy.
